log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought: Plan: lead Garchomp (Mega option), with Gholdengo and Kingambit behind. Opponent has Incineroar, Garchomp, Gholdengo, Sinistcha, Corviknight, Dragapult.

Plan: Lead Incineroar for Intimidate and Fake Out. Garchomp (Mega) is the main sweeper; keep it away from Kingambit and Corviknight's Steel typing. Gholdengo covers Dragapult and Corviknight with special attacks. Opponent threats: Dragapult (fast, Infiltrator/Clear Body), Kingambit (Defiant), Gholdengo, Garchomp (Rough Skin or Sand Veil), Incineroar, Corviknight. Watch for Kingambit's Defiant and Dragapult's speed.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Looking at the matchup, I need to pick three from my team against their Kingambit, Gholdengo, Incineroar, Garchomp, Dragapult, and Corviknight. I'm leaning toward Incineroar for intimidate and Fake Out support, Garchomp as a strong mega attacker, and Gholdengo for special pressure, though Corviknight could also work well defensively against their Kingambit and Garchomp.

decisions.thought: Lead Garchomp vs Incineroar (Intimidate, my Atk -1). Mega Evolve now and use Earthquake, since Incineroar is weak to Ground. Keep Gholdengo and Kingambit in the back. Watch for Incineroar's Flare Blitz, Knock Off and U-turn.

Battle start: I led Incineroar (Intimidate dropped their Garchomp's Atk). Opposing Garchomp is faster than my Incineroar, so Fake Out now to flinch it and chip damage. Plan: keep Garchomp away from Kingambit/Corviknight Steel typing, use Gholdengo specials against Dragapult and Corviknight, and watch for Kingambit's Defiant and Dragapult's speed. Opponent may Mega Garchomp (item unknown).
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Opening with Incineroar's Fake Out on the opposing Garchomp since it's turn one and legal—neutral damage plus a flinch, regardless of whether it's holding Garchompite.

decisions.thought: Turn 2: Mega Garchomp (Atk -1) vs Incineroar, which used Fake Out. Earthquake is super effective. Watch for Flare Blitz, Knock Off and U-turn. Keep Gholdengo and Kingambit in the back. Their Gholdengo has Good as Gold, so my status moves won't work on it.

Opponent Mega Garchomp (Sand Force) is at 86% with Atk -1. Its speed is probably below my Garchomp's 169, so my Garchomp outspeeds it. Plan: Parting Shot to drop its Atk and SpA, then bring in Garchomp to Mega next turn and attack first. Flare Blitz does only 0.5x to Dragon. Watch for Kingambit's Defiant, Dragapult's speed, and Corviknight's Steel typing. Gholdengo handles Dragapult and Corviknight later.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Mega Garchomp is at 86% HP with its attack lowered, and it flinched this turn thanks to Sand Force boosting its power. Since Incineroar is slower, I need to anticipate Garchomp hitting it with something like Earthquake, Dragon Claw, or Stone Edge next turn.

Flare Blitz on Garchomp would be weak given its typing, so I'm weighing Parting Shot to further cripple its stats while swapping to either Gholdengo or my own Garchomp -- though Gholdengo is vulnerable to Earthquake too. Protect doesn't seem worth it here, and I'm also considering whether Mega Evolving my own Garchomp is even an option this turn given the circumstances.

My Garchomp at 169 speed should outpace their Mega Garchomp even at its highest possible stat range, so switching in and setting up with Swords Dance looks promising. Parting Shot into Garchomp means it'll eat an Earthquake on entry, but with their Attack dropped twice the damage should be manageable given my bulk; alternatively, switching to Gholdengo with Life Orb is still on the table.

The simplest line is to Parting Shot now to tank their offenses, then bring in Garchomp, which outspeeds and can threaten with Earthquake or Stone Edge in the mirror matchup. Going with Parting Shot.

decisions.thought: Opponent Mega Garchomp (86%, Atk -2, SpA -1) is now the main threat. Its Earthquake is 2x on Incineroar (Fire/Dark), so Incineroar at 84 HP is at risk. Switching in Garchomp (Spe 169) is safer: Earthquake is only neutral on Dragon/Ground Garchomp, and Garchomp outspeeds. Next: Garchomp attacks (Earthquake or Dragon Claw) or Swords Dance if safe. Save Gholdengo for Dragapult and Corviknight. Kingambit Defiant and Dragapult speed are still unknown threats.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar's at 84/202 HP while the Mega Garchomp opponent sits at 86% with lowered Attack and Special Attack. My Garchomp outspeeds at 169 versus their 100-158, so I'm weighing a switch in, checking whether their Earthquake would be dangerous against my own Garchomp given it holds the Garchompite.

Mega isn't available to me since only one Mega is allowed per battle and the opponent already used theirs. Earthquake against my Garchomp is actually just neutral damage since Ground doesn't hit Dragon/Ground super effectively, so switching in seems safer than I first thought — the alternative is keeping Incineroar in to use a status or support move instead.

Incineroar's already at -2 attack from Parting Shot, and it's taken a big Earthquake hit as Fire/Dark since Ground is 2x against Fire; another hit would likely knock it out. Switching to Garchomp makes more sense since it outspeeds the opponent's Mega Garchomp and takes Earthquake neutrally, letting me set up with Swords Dance or attack with Stone Edge instead.

decisions.thought: Turn 3: My Mega Garchomp is at Atk -2 and SpA -1, so I'm switching to Gholdengo to take on their Garchomp (they just brought it in). Their Incineroar is at 41% and has used Fake Out and Parting Shot, so Garchomp may come back later as a Ground attacker once it is no longer debuffed. Keep Kingambit as a late-game cleaner. Their Gholdengo has Good as Gold.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With my Garchomp lowered in both attacking stats, I'm weighing switching to Gholdengo, but its Steel typing is weak to Ground, so an Earthquake from the opposing Garchomp would hurt badly.

Kingambit's Sucker Punch could work too, but it's only moderate damage given its stats. Gholdengo is the better switch here.

decisions.thought: Opponent Mega Garchomp (Sand Force, Atk -2, SpA -1, about 86% HP) is the main threat. Its Earthquake is neutral on my Garchomp. Dragon Claw is super effective on Garchomp and gets STAB, so it outdamages Earthquake. Mega-evolving raises my Atk from 182 to about 222. Mega Garchomp has Sand Force, not Sand Stream, so it won't set sand. Keep Gholdengo for Dragapult and Corviknight, and watch for Kingambit's Defiant.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm assessing the matchup: my Garchomp versus their Mega Garchomp at 86% health with Atk -2 and SpA -1 stages, noting its Sand Force ability boosts Ground moves like Earthquake, though it hits neutrally since my Garchomp is also part Ground-type.

Comparing my options against their Garchomp at ~160 HP: Earthquake is neutral STAB at 100 effective BP, but Dragon Claw gets a dragon-on-dragon super-effective hit at 80 BP doubled to 160 effective — making Dragon Claw the stronger choice despite lower base power.

I'm weighing whether to Mega Evolve now. Roughskin matters against contact moves, but their Garchomp's Earthquake isn't contact, so losing that ability costs little; meanwhile Mega Garchomp's stat boost looks significant enough to justify evolving, assuming the listed stats already reflect the mega form.

Mega boosts Atk substantially, and since the opponent's Garchomp is already Mega, mine should Mega too—going with dragonclaw as Mega, accepting the loss of Rough Skin for Sand Force since it's still worth it.

decisions.thought: Mega Garchomp (Sand Force) outspeeds their Gholdengo (76% HP, Leftovers, Good as Gold). Earthquake is super effective on Steel and should KO it. Their Garchomp is down to 86% and is the bigger threat, so if it returns I'll need to handle it. Kingambit (Defiant), Dragapult (speed), and Corviknight remain unknown. Keep Gholdengo for Dragapult and Corviknight.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Garchomp is at full HP against their Gholdengo sitting at 76% with leftovers. Since Gholdengo is Steel/Ghost, Earthquake hits it super effectively, and with Garchomp's strong Attack stat this should deal heavy damage to their remaining ~135 HP.

Running the numbers, Earthquake with STAB-less 2x effectiveness should land somewhere around 130-150+ damage, which is enough to KO Gholdengo even on a low roll. Since I'm already faster anyway, Earthquake is the clear play here.

decisions.thought: Turn 4: Their Mega Garchomp is at full HP. Its Dragon Claw is resisted by my Gholdengo, but Earthquake would be super effective, and it may outspeed me. I'm attacking with Make It Rain. My Mega Garchomp is at Atk -2 and SpA -1, so I'll keep it as a Ground-immune... no, it isn't immune; Kingambit stays as a late cleaner. Their Incineroar is at 41% and has used Fake Out and Parting Shot. Their Gholdengo has Good as Gold.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Against Mega Garchomp, I'm checking type matchups for Gholdengo—Steel/Ghost resists Dragon Claw but is weak to Earthquake, and Garchomp lacks weather support since Sand Force needs sandstorm that isn't active here.

Gholdengo's Make It Rain would deal solid but not lethal damage, maybe 65-70%, while Garchomp's Earthquake could potentially one-shot my Gholdengo given its Steel-type 2x weakness and likely speed advantage. I'm puzzled why they used Dragon Claw instead of Earthquake, wondering if it was a misprediction about which Pokémon would switch in.

Considering alternatives, switching to Kingambit exposes me to a super-effective Earthquake, and switching to my own Garchomp means eating a 2x Dragon Claw while EQ stays neutral. Attacking now with Make It Rain or Shadow Ball seems like the better line, even with the SpA drop risk, since staying in and dying to EQ is likely regardless of my choice if they outspeed.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo fainted. Their Mega Garchomp is at full HP and has Dragon Claw and Earthquake. Their Incineroar is at 41% with Fake Out and Parting Shot. My Mega Garchomp has Atk -2 and SpA -1. Kingambit would nearly die to Earthquake, so keep it as the late cleaner. Their last Pokémon is one of Gholdengo, Sinistcha, Corviknight or Dragapult. Their Gholdengo has Good as Gold.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Gholdengo just fainted, so I need to pick a switch-in against their full-health Mega Garchomp. Weighing mega Garchomp with its stat drops against Kingambit, checking whether Kingambit's Dark/Steel moves like Kowtow Cleave, Iron Head, or Sucker Punch actually threaten it.

Earthquake would hit Kingambit hard, probably enough to knock it out or get it dangerously low, and Garchomp outspeeds. My own Garchomp at -2 attack and only neutral Dragon Claw damage looks too weak to be useful here, so Kingambit seems like the only real option despite the EQ risk.

My Dragon Claw only does about 42% to their Garchomp, while their Earthquake does 94-111 to my side, so both trades are ugly. Sacrificing a mon seems unavoidable either way, and even if Kingambit's Sucker Punch gets a chunk in, Mega Garchomp still takes a big hit and leaves me stuck with Kingambit facing their Garchomp alone, which isn't a good spot. I should consider keeping Garchomp back instead and using it differently.

decisions.thought: Turn 5: My Mega Garchomp (full HP) faces their Mega Garchomp (86%, Sand Force, Earthquake revealed). Dragon Claw is super effective on it and gets STAB, so it's my best damage. Their Garchomp's Earthquake is neutral on mine. Their remaining 3 possible: Kingambit (Defiant?), Dragapult, Corviknight. Gholdengo is in the back for Dragapult/Corviknight. Incineroar (84 HP) should stay out of Earthquake range.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: My Mega Garchomp is at full health against their Mega Garchomp at 86%, and they've already revealed Earthquake. I'm checking Dragon Claw's effectiveness since Dragon hits Dragon for super effective damage, calculating the damage with my 222 Attack against their likely Defense stat.

decisions.thought: Their Mega Garchomp has Dragon Claw and Earthquake, and probably KOs my debuffed Mega Garchomp (Atk -2). Use it to chip damage, then bring Kingambit in for free after it faints. Their Incineroar (41%) has Fake Out and Parting Shot. Their last Pokémon is unknown.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Mega Garchomp is at Atk -2, SpA -1, with 160/185 HP, facing their full-health Mega Garchomp with Sand Force in a no-weather field. I'm checking speed tiers between the two megas, then working out how much Dragon Claw would deal given my lowered attack stat.

Their Dragon Claw against my mega could deal around 165-170 damage based on the earlier Gholdengo comparison, which would likely knock me out at 160 HP regardless of who moves first. Switching to Kingambit is risky too since Earthquake hits for 2x against its Dark/Steel typing, though Dragon Claw would only be neutral on it, so I'm weighing whether they're more likely to click Dragon Claw or Earthquake next.

Better plan: let Garchomp attack and go down fighting rather than switch out, since if it dies Kingambit can come in free without eating a hit. Dragon Claw seems the right call here over Rockslide's weak flinch chance.

decisions.note: Only one legal action: played without asking.

decisions.thought: Their Mega Garchomp is at 18% with Dragon Claw and Earthquake. Sucker Punch (priority) should KO it. Their Incineroar is at 41% with Fake Out and Parting Shot. Their last Pokémon is one of Gholdengo, Sinistcha, Corviknight or Dragapult. Kingambit has Supreme Overlord at +20%.

Mega Garchomp (35 HP, faster than Kingambit) moves first. Earthquake is super effective on Kingambit (Dark/Steel) and should KO or nearly KO it. Kingambit's Supreme Overlord boosts its power, and its Defiant may trigger from my Incineroar's Intimidate. Watch for Dragapult and Corviknight next; Gholdengo (full HP) is the answer to them. Incineroar (84 HP, Sitrus used) should stay out of Kingambit's attacks.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: My Mega Garchomp outspeeds Kingambit, who just got a Supreme Overlord boost from a fainted ally. Since Earthquake hits Kingambit's Steel typing super effectively, I'm checking if the STAB Ground attack has enough power to knock it out given its bulky defense stat.

decisions.thought: Mega Garchomp fainted. Opponent's last Pokemon is Kingambit (90%, Life Orb, Supreme Overlord, Sucker Punch seen). I'm switching in Incineroar: Dark resists Kingambit's Dark attacks, and Flare Blitz is super effective on Steel, so it should threaten a KO next turn. Gholdengo takes double damage from Dark moves, so it stays in the back. Incineroar has 84 HP and no item.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Garchomp just fainted, and the opponent's last remaining Pokémon is Kingambit at 90% with Life Orb, having already used Supreme Overlord and revealed Sucker Punch. With their Garchomp and Gholdengo both down, I'm left deciding whether to bring in Incineroar at 84 HP to close this out.

Checking the matchup against Gholdengo: Shadow Ball gets resisted by Dark, but Thunderbolt hits neutrally since Steel doesn't resist Electric, so that's a solid option if I go this route. Still, Kingambit's Sucker Punch could threaten Gholdengo first given the priority and its boosted Attack from Supreme Overlord.

Looking at Incineroar instead, its Dark typing resists Kingambit's Sucker Punch, but Flare Blitz hits Kingambit's Steel typing for super effective damage with STAB, likely dealing massive damage given Incineroar's strong Attack stat.

Sucker Punch would be resisted by Incineroar's Dark typing and likely doesn't KO, but if Kingambit outspeeds (its base speed can exceed Incineroar's 80), it attacks first regardless of priority. I should also factor in Intimidate triggering on Kingambit's switch-in, which would lower its Attack and boost Defiant, somewhat offsetting the Atk drop.

Comparing Gholdengo's options against Kingambit, Shadow Ball is halved by Dark typing and Gholdengo is doubly weak to Sucker Punch, making it a worse pick. Since Garchomp fainted I'm forced into a switch rather than an attack, so Incineroar is the better choice here given its resistance to Dark and strong Fire-type follow-up with Flare Blitz next turn.

decisions.thought: Turn 7: Kingambit (90%, Life Orb, Attack -1 from Intimidate) is their last Pokemon. Flare Blitz is super effective on it and should threaten a KO. Incineroar has 84 HP and no item, so Sucker Punch could hurt. Gholdengo stays in the back because Dark moves hit it hard. If Incineroar survives, Flare Blitz again, or Parting Shot to switch into Gholdengo for a Make It Rain / Shadow Ball attack.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm noting Kingambit at 90% with Life Orb and an attack drop from Intimidate, wondering whether Defiant should've triggered that boost instead — it might actually be Pressure or Supreme Overlord at play here. Sucker Punch is still a threat to watch for against Incineroar.

Calculating Flare Blitz's damage on Kingambit: Fire hits Steel super effectively, so even at -1 Attack this looks like a likely KO given Kingambit's HP and bulk. Sucker Punch back from Kingambit is risky but weaker in comparison, so sending in Incineroar and firing off Flare Blitz seems like the strongest play despite the recoil.

decisions.thought: Turn 7: Kingambit is at 90% with Atk -1 and Supreme Overlord at +20%. Their Incineroar (41%) has Fake Out and Parting Shot. Fake Out should flinch me this turn, so Swords Dance costs nothing. Dark and Steel moves are both resisted by Incineroar, so I need boosts. Their last Pokémon is one of Gholdengo, Sinistcha, Corviknight or Dragapult.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking type matchups for Kingambit's moves against Incineroar—Iron Head gets resisted by Fire typing, while Kowtow Cleave against Dark is also resisted, so I'm weighing which attack hits harder given Incineroar's dual typing.

Running the damage math, neither Kowtow Cleave (~51) nor Sucker Punch (~43) can knock out Incineroar's remaining ~78 HP, and since Fake Out will flinch Kingambit this turn before it can act, I can't use that turn to set up with Swords Dance either.

Weighing my options: if Incineroar goes for Fake Out, whatever I pick doesn't matter since I flinch anyway, so there's no cost to choosing Swords Dance — if they attack instead, it still boosts me to net +1 after the stat drop, while Sucker Punch risks whiffing entirely against a Parting Shot switch. Swords Dance seems like the safer pick here.

decisions.thought: Kingambit is their last Pokemon at 3% HP with Life Orb, +1 Attack, and Sucker Punch (priority, works because it attacked or used Swords Dance). Incineroar has 25 HP and may be outsped. Protect (+4 priority) blocks Sucker Punch and any other attack this turn. Life Orb recoil should finish Kingambit if it attacks at 3%. Next turn, Flare Blitz or Gholdengo can finish it.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking the matchup: Kingambit at 3% HP with net +1 Attack from Swords Dance/Intimidate, versus Incineroar at 25 HP. Since Incineroar is Fire/Dark, its own Sucker Punch would be resisted by its Dark typing, so I need to factor that into the damage calc.

If Kingambit is faster, Sucker Punch likely finishes Incineroar even resisted; if Incineroar is faster, its Flare Blitz kills Kingambit first. Protect could stall Sucker Punch, but Kingambit attacking next turn with Life Orb recoil at 3% HP would cause it to faint from the recoil regardless of the outcome.

decisions.thought: Kingambit is at 7 HP, so Life Orb recoil will KO it after any attack. Sucker Punch kills Incineroar first, but I likely lose to their last Pokémon regardless.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm calculating whether Kingambit's Sucker Punch can finish off Incineroar at 12% HP, factoring in its boosted Attack, Life Orb, and Supreme Overlord bonus against Incineroar's resistance to the dark-type move.

That damage easily exceeds Incineroar's remaining HP, so the KO lands as long as Incineroar actually attacks rather than using a status move like Parting Shot. But Life Orb recoil is roughly 20 HP, more than Kingambit's own 7 HP, so Kingambit would faint right after landing the kill, which means I need to think through what that mutual knockout means for who actually wins the game.

Checking recoil math — with 7 HP, Life Orb recoil would be minimal and Incineroar survives Sucker Punch at 12%. Realistically there's no winning line here: killing Incineroar just leaves me fainting to recoil while their last Pokémon remains, so I'm just looking for the best practical option rather than an actual win, considering whether they might switch out of Sucker Punch's range.

decisions.thought: Kingambit is at 7 HP with Life Orb, so any attack I make will KO me through recoil. Their Incineroar is at 12% and likely attacks this turn. Sucker Punch should KO it first. I probably lose to their last Pokémon afterwards.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Kingambit is at 7 HP with +1 Attack after the Intimidate/Swords Dance exchange, facing Incineroar at 12% HP. Since Incineroar already used Protect last turn and has been out too long for Fake Out, it'll likely attack directly—Flare Blitz would kill me, so I need to consider Sucker Punch as my response.

Sucker Punch should easily knock out Incineroar's remaining HP even though it's resisted, but the Life Orb recoil from my own attack would then finish off my already-critical Kingambit. That leaves me with no Pokémon left while my opponent still has one remaining, meaning I lose regardless—unless they switch out, which would cause Sucker Punch to fail entirely. There's no way around this outcome; Sucker Punch is still my best option since Kowtow Cleave carries the same fatal recoil problem.

decisions.thought: Kingambit is at 3% with Life Orb and +1 Attack. Incineroar has 25 HP, and Sucker Punch could KO it if Kingambit moves first. Switching to Gholdengo (164 HP, speed 149) is safe: it outspeeds Kingambit, survives a Sucker Punch, and KOs it next turn. Next turn, use Make It Rain or Shadow Ball to finish Kingambit. Its Dark moves hit Gholdengo hard, so keep it out of range after that.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Kingambit is nearly dead at 3% with Life Orb and +1 Attack, while Incineroar sits at 25 HP. It comes down to speed: if Incineroar outpaces Kingambit, Flare Blitz finishes it off, but if Kingambit moves first, Sucker Punch from its boosted Attack likely knocks out Incineroar instead.

Wait, if Protect blocks Sucker Punch, the move fails entirely, so Life Orb recoil shouldn't trigger since no damage was dealt—Kingambit stays at 3% and the standoff could repeat next turn. Flare Blitz would avoid this issue if I'm faster, since recoil still applies even on a KO, but at least the Kingambit threat would already be eliminated.

Considering Flare Blitz speed matchups, Kingambit's speed range overlaps dangerously, and Sucker Punch only works if I attack, so going for Flare Blitz is risky if Kingambit outspeeds. Switching to Gholdengo looks safer instead—Dark hits it neutrally through Steel typing despite the Ghost weakness, so it should survive a Sucker Punch easily and then finish Kingambit off with Make It Rain or Shadow Ball.

decisions.thought: Kingambit is at 3% with Life Orb and +1 Attack, and Gholdengo (speed 149) outspeeds it. Thunderbolt is the most damaging option here: Electric is neutral on Dark/Steel, while Ghost and Steel moves are not very effective. Any hit should KO. If the battle continues, Gholdengo should avoid Dark moves, and Incineroar at 25 HP should stay back.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Kingambit is down to 3% with Life Orb and +1 Attack, but Gholdengo outspeeds it easily. Since Kingambit is Dark/Steel, Shadow Ball hits super effectively through its Ghost typing, so that's the move to finish it off.

Thunderbolt is clearly the best choice here since any move likely secures the kill at such low health anyway, and the paralysis chance is just a bonus with full accuracy. Going with thunderbolt.

decisions.thought: Turn 10: Kingambit has 7 HP and Life Orb, so any attack I make faints me through recoil. The only line is Sucker Punch, which KOs Gholdengo if it attacks. Their Incineroar (12%) remains, so this is likely a loss anyway.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Kingambit at 7 HP against full-health Gholdengo, any attack risks Life Orb recoil killing me, so I need Sucker Punch's priority to strike first since Gholdengo otherwise outspeeds and kills me. I'm calculating the Sucker Punch damage with my Attack boost and Supreme Overlord bonus from the fainted ally.

Running the numbers with Kingambit's Dark STAB and Steel weakness factored in, I find Sucker Punch comfortably OHKOs Gholdengo across its likely defense range, but the Life Orb recoil would then faint me simultaneously since I only have 7 HP. The risk is if Gholdengo uses Nasty Plot instead of attacking—Sucker Punch would fail and deal no damage, but at least I'd survive that turn without recoil since the move didn't connect.

With Incineroar still alive at 12% on the opponent's side, even trading Gholdengo for myself likely means I lose anyway since they'd have the last Pokémon standing. There's no real winning line here, so I'll just go with Sucker Punch as the best shot—it at least guarantees a kill if Gholdengo attacks, and costs nothing extra if it doesn't.
